item.title: Urban Intensification in Geelong: How Resident Beliefs and Attitudes Shape Responses to Planning Proposals
item.dc:title: Urban Intensification in Geelong: How Resident Beliefs and Attitudes Shape Responses to Planning Proposals
item.dc:creator: Suzanne Barker Carl Grodach Urban Planning and Design, Monash University, Caulfield Campus, Caulfield, AustraliaSuzanne Barker is a Senior Lecturer in Urban Planning and Design at Monash University. Her research examines how planning, design and participatory processes shape people’s experience of urban change, with particular interest in community infrastructure, social connection, civic infrastructuring and the role of the built environment in creating opportunities for encounter. Her work draws on behavioral insights, place attachment and participatory approaches to understand how communities engage with planning and development. Suzanne brings over two decades of professional planning experience to her research and teaching spanning strategic and growth planning, urban design, community engagement and governance.Carl Grodach is a Foundation Professor of Urban Planning and Design at Monash University. His research focuses on economic development planning with an emphasis on urban manufacturing and industrial lands, cultural industries, and circular economies. His books include Urban Revitalization: Remaking Cities in a Changing World (Routledge) and The Politics of Urban Cultural Policy: Global Perspectives (Routledge). He was the inaugural director of Monash Urban Planning and Design from 2017–2022.
